extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and persons subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO, focusing on execution of inventor declarations, applicable disciplinary rule violations, jurisdictional authority, settlement procedure requirements, and possible sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Declaration signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. §115 recites that the applicant shall make oath that he believes himself to be the original and first inventor ... 35 U.S.C. §25 recites that a Declaration may be submitted in lieu of oath; however, whenever such written declaration is used, the document must warn the declarant that willful false statements ... are punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both (18 U.S.C. §1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Declaration for Utility or Design Application must be executed by each inventor (i.e., the signature of each inventor is required) unless the application is being filed under 37 C.F.R. §1.47. When a Declaration is used in lieu of oath it must include the statutory warning language of 18 U.S.C. §1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor execution cannot be replaced by practitioner signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Declaration in the '612 application was executed by Respondent and not by the inventors; Respondent believed at the time, albeit erroneously, that annotating the document with the word 'Agent' was appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner must not sign an inventor's declaration (even if annotating the signature with 'Agent'); the practitioner's electronic signature in place of inventor signatures is improper and violates USPTO rules (see 37 C.F.R. §11.18 as governing changes to representation/filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include 18 U.S.C. §1001 warning when using declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a written declaration is used in lieu of oath the document must warn the declarant that willful false statements ... are punishable by fine or imprisonment, or both (18 U.S.C. §1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the declaration submitted contains the required criminal false-statement warning language; absence or incorrect execution of this statutory language affects the validity and acceptability of the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 37 C.F.R. §1.47 exception
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no evidence that the '612 application was being filed under 37 C.F.R. §1.47. Therefore, the signature of each inventor was required on the Declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is properly filed under 37 C.F.R. §1.47, different signature/filing rules may apply; absent that, inventor signatures are mandatory on declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary grounds under 37 C.F.R. §10.23
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(5) by engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice; §10.23(b)(6) by engaging in any conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office; and §10.23(c)(15) by signing a paper filed in the Office in violation of the provisions of §11.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct like improperly signing filings or filing papers in violation of USPTO rules may be charged under multiple disciplinary subsections (prejudicial to administration of justice; adversely reflecting on fitness to practice; signing papers in violation of representation/filing rules) and can support sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited signing in violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.18
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order notes the practitioner signed a paper filed in the Office in violation of the provisions of §11.18 (Changes to Representation of Others Before the Patent and Trademark Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must follow §11.18 rules regarding who may sign submissions and how representation/authorization is recorded; failure to comply can form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. §11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement ... satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.26, resolves all disciplinary action ... and sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements in OED matters must meet §11.26 requirements and should include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions; once approved by the USPTO Director, they resolve the disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction to discipline practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§11.20(a)(3) and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO Director (and OED) derive authority from statute and regulation to investigate and impose discipline on registered practitioners; practitioners before the Office are subject to these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and imposed for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered sanctions: (a) Respondent is publicly reprimanded; (b) The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; (c) The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette; (d) The OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public; (e) The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary consequences for violations can include public reprimand, publication in the Official Gazette, notices to other disciplinary agencies and courts, and specified allocation of costs; settlement agreements may specify these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to correct regulatory citations and note rule transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement inadvertently references 37 C.F.R. §10.18. The correct reference is to 37 C.F.R. §11.18. Changes to Representation of Others Before the Patent and Trademark Office, Final Rule; Correction ... explaining that the substance of §10.18 was transferred to §11.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing regulations, practitioners and OED documents must use current and correct regulatory citations; be aware of historical transfers of rule substance (e.g., §10.18 → §11.18) and correct inadvertent miscitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS-Web filings must accurately reflect POA and inventor signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: A Power of Attorney or Authorization of Agent was filed with the USPTO via EFS-Web ... and a Declaration for Utility or Design Application was filed in the '612 application via EFS-Web ... Respondent's electronic signature was submitted for each of the named inventors, annotated by the word 'Agent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using EFS-Web to file POAs and declarations, ensure the filings correctly record the inventors' own signatures (or proper alternatives) and that practitioner signatures/annotations do not substitute for inventor execution; improper electronic signing can result in disciplinary action.
